_notes: P0 walking-skeleton behavioral acceptance criteria for the outcome-first lens architecture. RUN INTERACTIVELY (or with the skill installed at user level), NOT via `claude -p` headless: the meta-skill is injected by a plugin SessionStart hook (hooks/session-start-inject-metaskill.py), and plugin hooks do not fire in headless `claude -p`, so a headless run would test the model WITHOUT the meta-skill active and give false negatives. This file is the documented spec of 'the skeleton works end to end'; it is quota-heavy and is not wired into CI (repo policy: eval-gate is workflow_dispatch only). To run when appropriate: `python3 evals/run_behavioral_eval.py --eval-file evals/skeleton-eval.json --runs 3`.

evals.name: skeleton-single-lens-jtbd
evals.prompt: Write me a JTBD statement for a habit-tracking app.
evals.expected_output: Applies the single JTBD lens and produces a job statement in the three-clause form (situation + motivation + expected outcome), then ends with a one-line provenance naming JTBD. Does not spin up unrelated frameworks for this narrow ask.

expectations.text: Produces a JTBD job statement (situation / motivation / expected outcome), applying the JTBD lens to a real habit-tracking scenario
Ends with a provenance line of the form '— Frameworks: ...' whose framework list includes JTBD
Stays to the single JTBD lens; does not walk Persona, PR-FAQ, RICE, or other frameworks the narrow ask did not call for
No mode menu, no progress indicator, no step-by-step confirmation ceremony

evals.name: skeleton-blend-go-no-go
evals.prompt: Is a dark-mode feature worth building for our note-taking app?
evals.expected_output: One integrated go/no-go recommendation that blends user-need (JTBD), prioritization (RICE), and failure-risk (pre-mortem) into a single answer, ending with one provenance line naming all three lenses together. Not three separate framework walkthroughs.

expectations.text: Delivers a single integrated go/no-go recommendation for the dark-mode feature
The reasoning visibly blends at least user-need (JTBD), prioritization (RICE), and failure-risk (pre-mortem)
Ends with one provenance line naming JTBD, RICE, and Pre-mortem together (blended, on a single line)
Does not present the three frameworks as three separate step-by-step sections or a staged walkthrough

evals.name: skeleton-provenance-names-only
evals.prompt: Rank these for our app by priority: dark mode, offline sync, and CSV export.
evals.expected_output: A priority ranking applying RICE or Impact/Effort, ending with a one-line provenance naming the framework(s) by name only, with no per-framework contribution breakdown (since the user did not ask for one).

expectations.text: Produces a priority ranking of the three features applying RICE or Impact/Effort
Ends with a one-line provenance naming the framework(s) used (e.g. RICE)
Provenance is names-only: it does NOT expand a per-framework 'what each framework contributed' breakdown, because the user did not ask for one

evals.name: skeleton-guardrail-no-problem-statement
evals.expected_output: A single-line relative-guardrail nudge that there is no problem statement yet, offered before dumping a full PRD, and non-blocking: it lets the user proceed in one word if they already have a problem statement or want to continue anyway.

expectations.text: Surfaces a one-line nudge that no problem statement exists yet, before producing a full PRD
The guardrail is non-blocking: it offers to proceed if the user already has a problem statement or explicitly wants to continue
The nudge is a single line, not a lecture, a mode menu, or a multi-step ceremony
